chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is upon the Muhrim (one in Ihram) to be watchful of the locusts if they are on his path; if he finds no alternative, he may kill them, and there is no objection.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram if they encounter locusts on their path?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar clarifies that the prohibition of killing game in Ihram does not extend to locusts, which are considered non-game insects. Shaykh al-Tusi presents this as a case of necessity (darura), where the pilgrim is exempt from penalty only when killing is unavoidable, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship in ritual purity and conduct.
